subChunks.title: Progressive Web Apps (PWA) with React
subChunks.hookHtml: A Progressive Web App is a website that earns installation rights — it loads instantly from cache, works offline, receives push notifications, and can be added to the home screen like a native app. With Vite's PWA plugin, turning a React app into a PWA is primarily configuration: define what to cache, what the manifest should say, and let the service worker handle the rest.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Vite PWA plugin setup

// vite.config.ts:
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';
import { VitePWA } from 'vite-plugin-pwa';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    react(),
    VitePWA({
      registerType: 'autoUpdate',
      includeAssets: ['favicon.svg', 'robots.txt', 'apple-touch-icon.png'],
      manifest: {
        name: 'Arcane Academy',
        short_name: 'Arcane',
        description: 'Master the arcane arts of React',
        theme_color: '#1a1a2e',
        background_color: '#1a1a2e',
        display: 'standalone',
        icons: [
          { src: 'pwa-192x192.png', sizes: '192x192', type: 'image/png' },
          { src: 'pwa-512x512.png', sizes: '512x512', type: 'image/png' },
          { src: 'pwa-512x512.png', sizes: '512x512', type: 'image/png', purpose: 'any maskable' },
        ],
      },
      workbox: {
        globPatterns: ['**/*.{js,css,html,ico,png,svg}'],
        runtimeCaching: [
          {
            urlPattern: /^https:\/\/api\.arcane\.academy\/.*/,
            handler: 'NetworkFirst',
            options: {
              cacheName: 'api-cache',
              expiration: { maxEntries: 100, maxAgeSeconds: 86400 },
              networkTimeoutSeconds: 10,
            },
          },
        ],
      },
    }),
  ],
});

Caching strategies

// Workbox provides four main strategies:

// CacheFirst — serve from cache, update in background:
// Use for: fonts, images, app shell, static assets
// Risk: stale content served until cache expires

// NetworkFirst — try network, fall back to cache:
// Use for: API responses, dynamic content
// Risk: slow when network is slow (waits for timeout)

// StaleWhileRevalidate — serve cache instantly, update in background:
// Use for: user avatars, non-critical API data
// Benefit: fast + eventually fresh

// NetworkOnly — always fetch, never cache:
// Use for: POST mutations, payment endpoints, auth

Offline detection and UI

import { useRegisterSW } from 'virtual:pwa-register/react';

function PWAUpdatePrompt() {
  const { needRefresh, updateServiceWorker } = useRegisterSW({
    onRegistered(r) {
      console.log('SW registered:', r);
    },
    onRegisterError(error) {
      console.error('SW registration error:', error);
    },
  });

  return needRefresh ? (
    <div role="alert" className="update-banner">
      <p>New version available!</p>
      <button onClick={() => updateServiceWorker(true)}>Update now</button>
    </div>
  ) : null;
}

// Offline status hook:
function useOnlineStatus() {
  const [isOnline, setIsOnline] = useState(navigator.onLine);

  useEffect(() => {
    const handleOnline = () => setIsOnline(true);
    const handleOffline = () => setIsOnline(false);
    window.addEventListener('online', handleOnline);
    window.addEventListener('offline', handleOffline);
    return () => {
      window.removeEventListener('online', handleOnline);
      window.removeEventListener('offline', handleOffline);
    };
  }, []);

  return isOnline;
}

Background sync for offline mutations

// Queue mutations that fail offline, replay when back online:
async function acceptQuestWithSync(questId: string) {
  try {
    await fetch(`/api/quests/${questId}/accept`, { method: 'POST' });
  } catch {
    // Store in IndexedDB for later:
    const db = await openDB('sync-queue', 1);
    await db.add('pending-mutations', {
      type: 'ACCEPT_QUEST',
      payload: { questId },
      timestamp: Date.now(),
    });

    // Register for background sync:
    const sw = await navigator.serviceWorker.ready;
    await sw.sync.register('sync-mutations');
  }
}

// Service worker handles 'sync' event and replays mutations

Push notifications

async function subscribeToPushNotifications() {
  const registration = await navigator.serviceWorker.ready;

  const subscription = await registration.pushManager.subscribe({
    userVisibleOnly: true,
    applicationServerKey: urlBase64ToUint8Array(VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY),
  });

  // Send subscription to your server:
  await fetch('/api/push/subscribe', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify(subscription),
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  });
}

Vex: "A PWA is not a replacement for a native app — it's a website that earns installation. The bar is: fast first load, works offline for core features, has an icon and manifest. Caching strategy is the hard part: CacheFirst for static assets, NetworkFirst for API data, NetworkOnly for mutations. Never cache POST requests."

storyBeats.text: A guild member in a remote mountain pass loses signal mid-quest. The app goes blank — all that cached data, inaccessible. A service worker and an offline manifest later: the quest board loads from cache. The acceptance queues for background sync. The network returns; the mutation replays.

storyBeats.speaker: Vex the Interface Weaver
storyBeats.text: Service workers are JavaScript that runs in the background, separate from your app. They intercept every fetch request. You decide: serve from cache, fetch from network, or both. CacheFirst makes your app load instantly. NetworkFirst keeps data fresh. The manifest makes it installable. Together: a PWA.

storyBeats.speaker: Offline detection + UI feedback

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build offline awareness into a React app:

  • Create a useOnlineStatus() hook that listens to window online/offline events
  • Create an OfflineBanner component that renders only when offline with an accessible alert role
  • Write the Vite PWA plugin configuration with: NetworkFirst caching for /api/* routes, CacheFirst for static assets, and an app manifest for a quest tracker app
subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Turn the quest board into a full PWA: (1) Vite PWA plugin with a complete manifest (name, icons, theme colour, display: standalone). (2) NetworkFirst caching for API routes with a 10-second timeout and 24-hour cache expiry. (3) An OfflineBanner component with accessible role=alert and a specific message about what works offline vs what doesn't. (4) Background sync for quest acceptance — when offline, queue the mutation in IndexedDB and replay it when back online. Verify in Chrome DevTools > Application > Service Workers > Offline checkbox that the app loads and displays cached quests.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain what a service worker is — where does it run, what can it intercept, and why does it exist as a separate thread? Walk through the four Workbox caching strategies and give a real example of when you'd use each one. Explain why POST mutations should use NetworkOnly — what would happen if you cached a POST request for quest acceptance?

questions.prompt: Your PWA caches the quest list with StaleWhileRevalidate. A user accepts a quest offline, then comes online. The quest list still shows the quest as 'OPEN'. What is the problem?
options: StaleWhileRevalidate always serves the cached (stale) version first — the background revalidation runs, but the component doesn't re-render with the fresh data. Use NetworkFirst for mutable data that changes from user actions.
StaleWhileRevalidate doesn't work for authenticated endpoints
The service worker needs to be unregistered after offline mutations
The cache needs a shorter maxAgeSeconds to expire the stale entry
questions.answer: StaleWhileRevalidate always serves the cached (stale) version first — the background revalidation runs, but the component doesn't re-render with the fresh data. Use NetworkFirst for mutable data that changes from user actions.
questions.explanation: StaleWhileRevalidate is ideal for data where 'almost current' is good enough (avatars, public content, non-critical feeds). For user-specific data that changes based on user actions, NetworkFirst is safer: it tries the network first, waits up to networkTimeoutSeconds, then falls back to cache. This ensures the user sees their actual current state rather than a cached snapshot.

questions.prompt: A user's Stripe payment mutation is accidentally cached by the service worker. What could go wrong?
options: If the cached response is served instead of making a real network request, the user could be shown a success response from a previous payment while the new payment never actually processed — leading to a financial discrepancy
The payment would be charged twice because the cache replays the mutation
Service workers can't intercept HTTPS requests, so payment endpoints are safe
The browser will warn the user before serving a cached payment response
questions.answer: If the cached response is served instead of making a real network request, the user could be shown a success response from a previous payment while the new payment never actually processed — leading to a financial discrepancy
questions.explanation: POST mutations should always use NetworkOnly. If a payment endpoint returns a 200 and that response gets cached, the next payment attempt could be served from cache — the UI shows success, no money moves. Payment endpoints, authentication, and any state-changing operation must bypass the service worker entirely. In Workbox: urlPattern: /\/api\/payment/, handler: 'NetworkOnly'.
